evidence: evaluation_inputs.business_context.architectural_drivers has 5 named entries (BD-6..BD-10); each has at least one refined raw candidate scenario in the tree

evaluation_inputs.raw_candidate_scenarios has 16 entries; all 16 are refined into the tree under 8 quality attribute nodes, 3 of which (Security, Performance, Portability) have no named architectural driver
0 of 16 tree scenarios have a response measure: no raw scenario states a threshold and evaluation_inputs.quantitative_model_parameters.transaction_speed is qualitative ('Slow')
0 of 16 tree scenarios have a priority tuple: evaluation_inputs contains no stakeholder ranking of drivers or scenarios

gaps.description: RS-1 ('No unauthorized access to the system') states no response measure and no operating environment; the inputs name no actors, access paths or authorization mechanism.
gaps.missing_evidence: Who may access the system, through which interfaces, and how successful prevention or detection of unauthorized access is measured
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-1, which access attempts must be prevented and how is success measured (e.g. detection or rejection criteria)?

gaps.description: RS-2 ('fastest possible speed') states no load and no measurable target; evaluation_inputs.quantitative_model_parameters.performance_proxy names a proxy (number of components involved in a transaction) but gives no target value, and transaction_speed is only qualitative ('Slow').
gaps.missing_evidence: Event arrival rate or load level and an acceptable latency, throughput or component-count target
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-2, what event load applies and what latency, throughput or maximum number of components per transaction is acceptable?

gaps.description: RS-3 ('immediate recovery') names neither the failure types nor a recovery time or state to recover to.
gaps.missing_evidence: Failure types in scope, required recovery time and the state the system must recover to
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-3, which failures must be recovered from, within what time, and to what state?

gaps.description: RS-4 ('User errors in using system should be handled') does not state which user errors are in scope or what handling means (reject, report, recover).
gaps.missing_evidence: Classes of user error or invalid input and the required handling behavior and measure
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-4, which user errors or invalid inputs must be handled, and what observable response counts as handled?

gaps.description: RS-5 ('New demands on system functionality should be accommodated') states no concrete change, no effort or time bound, and no limit on affected components.
gaps.missing_evidence: An example functional change and an acceptable effort, time or number of components affected
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-5, what kind of new functionality is expected and what effort or scope of change is acceptable?

gaps.description: RS-6 ('Major parts of the framework should be re-usable') does not identify which parts are 'major' or how reuse is measured.
gaps.missing_evidence: The framework parts expected to be reused and a reuse criterion (e.g. reused without modification)
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-6, which framework parts must be reusable and what counts as successful reuse?

gaps.description: RS-7 ('cost-effective, fast and in minimal time') states no cost or time figure and no example modification.
gaps.missing_evidence: A representative modification and acceptable cost/effort and calendar time
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-7, which modification is representative and what cost and time limits apply?

gaps.description: RS-8 ('interact in a coordinated manner') does not define coordination or how it is checked.
gaps.missing_evidence: A definition of coordinated interaction (e.g. ordering or protocol rules) and an observable criterion
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-8, what observable property of component interaction counts as coordinated?

gaps.description: RS-9 ('more sophisticated options') does not name the options or a measure of expansion effort.
gaps.missing_evidence: Examples of the sophisticated options and acceptable expansion effort or impact
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-9, which options must the framework be expandable to support, and with what effort?

gaps.description: RS-10 ('execution in different environments') does not name the target environments or a porting measure.
gaps.missing_evidence: Target platforms or environments and acceptable porting effort
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-10, which environments must the implementation run in, and what porting effort is acceptable?

gaps.description: RS-11 ('Proper data encapsulation and secure data structures') names no data, threat or measurable criterion.
gaps.missing_evidence: The data to be protected, the threats or access paths, and a criterion for proper encapsulation
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-11, which data must be protected, from whom, and how is proper encapsulation judged?

gaps.description: RS-12 ('Flexible implementation using other programming languages') names no target languages or measure of flexibility.
gaps.missing_evidence: Target languages and an acceptable re-implementation effort or degree of design reuse
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-12, which other languages are expected and what counts as a flexible implementation?

gaps.description: RS-13 ('Overall consistent behavior') does not define consistency or the conditions under which it is assessed.
gaps.missing_evidence: A definition of consistent behavior and an observable criterion
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-13, what observable behavior must be consistent and under which conditions?

gaps.description: RS-14 ('complete, clear and perform exactly as required') refers to requirements that are not supplied in the inputs.
gaps.missing_evidence: The functional requirements of the framework and an acceptance criterion
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-14, which requirements define 'exactly as required', and how is completeness checked?

gaps.description: RS-15 ('Hook up multiple applications at same time') states neither how many applications nor whether this is a runtime or development-time concern, and gives no measure.
gaps.missing_evidence: Number of simultaneous applications, the phase (runtime or build) and an acceptance criterion
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-15, how many applications must be hooked up at once, at runtime or at build time, and what must hold when they are?

gaps.description: RS-16 ('Change interface from command-driven to window-based') gives no effort, time or scope limit for the change.
gaps.missing_evidence: Acceptable effort or time and the components allowed to change
gaps.resolution_question: For RS-16, what effort and which component changes are acceptable for moving from the CLI to a window-based interface?

gaps.description: Stakeholder prioritization is unavailable for RS-1, RS-2, RS-3, RS-4, RS-5, RS-6, RS-7, RS-8, RS-9, RS-10, RS-11, RS-12, RS-13, RS-14, RS-15 and RS-16: the inputs neither rank business goals or drivers (see G-1-5) nor rate scenario difficulty, so all priority tuples are null and analysis_order keeps input order (RS-1 to RS-16).
